title: Impact of Delayed Treatment on Progression of P. falciparum Malaria
author: Andria Mousa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgzfjx3n

steps.title: Conduct Literature Search
steps.instruction: Search Ovid MEDLINE and Embase for studies from inception to 22/11/2017 using the specified search strategy.

substeps.instruction: Use search terms: (malaria* or falciparum) AND (severe or cerebral) AND ((duration adj3 (illness or disease)) or delay* or access* or distance or travel* or case-control or risk factor or risk factors))
Search all terms in all fields with no restrictions on language or year of publication.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Perform study selection using EndNote X8, with decisions and extraction checked by a second reviewer.

substeps.instruction: Include studies containing data on severe disease, P. falciparum infection, and delay to treatment (duration of symptoms or fever prior to admission) for participants of any age and any language/year.

Exclude case reports, studies collecting data only on uncomplicated malaria, and studies with small total sample sizes (<100) unless they contain relevant data for comparing types of severe malarial disease.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Extract study-level data and request individual-participant data (IPD) from authors, managing the data using Microsoft Excel and Stata 14.

substeps.instruction: Extract: author names/contact details, country, transmission setting, ages, study design/matching, sample size, symptoms, inclusion/exclusion criteria, mean effect of delay, mortality, travel time/distance to facility, treatment type prior to admission, mother's education, and definitions for severe/uncomplicated malaria.
Request individual-level data and missing data from authors for studies that collected duration of illness but did not estimate the association with progression.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of included studies using the Newcastle Ottawa risk of bias tool for non-randomised studies.

substeps.instruction: Score studies separately based on the number of confounders measured, including age, travelling time/distance, and mother's education.

steps.title: Perform Pooled Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct age-adjusted, mixed-effects multivariable logistic regressions using Stata 14 to estimate ORs and 95% confidence intervals for risk of progression to severe malarial disease, specific types of severe disease, or mortality.

substeps.instruction: Stratify the main analysis by children (<15 years) and adults (15+ years).
Adjust for confounders: age, distance or travelling time to health facility, treatment prior to admission, transmission intensity of the setting, and mother's education.
Investigate effect modification by fitting interactions between the effect of delay and factors such as transmission intensity category or age.
